09:00.headline: Middle infielders: beyond the glove
09:00.topic: What coaches evaluate in middle infielders: hands/footwork, first step, throws on the run, home-to-first speed
09:00.caption:
Is your player a shortstop or second baseman? Coaches are watching more than whether he catches the ball.

When college coaches evaluate middle infielders, a few things come up again and again:

⚾ Hands and footwork: clean exchanges, balanced feet
⚾ First-step quickness: how fast he reads and reacts
⚾ Throws on the run: accuracy when he can't set his feet
⚾ Home-to-first speed: a measurable coaches can compare

Some of these show up best on video. Others, like home-to-first time, are numbers you can measure and track. Knowing where those numbers sit helps you see which levels (D1, D2, D3, NAIA or JUCO) fit him today.

Which of these is his strongest right now? 👇

13:00.headline: Hitters: more than exit velo
13:00.topic: What coaches evaluate in hitters: exit velo as a starting point for level fit, plus approach, swing decisions and results vs. good pitching
13:00.caption:
His exit velo is a great number to know. But is it the only thing a college coach looks at in a hitter?

Not usually. Exit velocity shows how hard he can hit the ball, and it's one of the clearest ways to compare him with typical ranges at each level.

Coaches also want to see:
✅ His approach: does he have a plan at the plate?
✅ Swing decisions: does he chase, or make pitchers work?
✅ Results against good pitching, not just batting practice

So use the number as a starting point. It helps you focus on the levels where he fits best. Then make sure his video and game results show the rest of the hitter.
